Chapter 6. The Echoes of the Past.
Sometimes, the past doesn’t just linger—it echoes. It shapes our present in ways we might not even realize, until life forces us to look over our shoulder and really see how far those echoes reach.
For Rie, searching for Daisuke’s real identity felt like stepping into the shadows of someone else’s life. It was a life he’d tried to keep hidden, but no matter how careful he was, it had never truly disappeared.
Kido’s investigation brought him to a faded photograph, tucked inside an old wallet. It wasn’t much—just a small picture—but it hinted at a different name, a different family. In the photo, a younger man stands beside a woman and a child. Their faces are blurred with time, but you can feel the connection between them. It’s a tiny window into a past Daisuke had left behind—a past that was once just as real as the life he’d built with Rie.
As Kido tried to follow the trail, things got tricky. Some doors opened with just a gentle nudge—a neighbor who remembered a quiet man who vanished one day, or a shopkeeper who thought back to a customer who always paid in cash. But other doors? They stayed tightly shut, locked away by silence and the slow march of years.
For Rie, every new discovery was bittersweet. There was relief in finding answers, but also a deep sadness—because each truth seemed to spark even more questions. What pain could have driven Daisuke to leave behind everything he knew? Was he running from something, or searching for something he’d lost? Those echoes from his past became a haunting refrain, reminding her that the people we love are shaped by moments and memories we may never fully uncover.
Most of us carry secrets. Some are small and harmless, but others are heavy enough to change the course of a life. It became clear to Rie that Daisuke’s choice to start over wasn’t just about hiding—it was a desperate attempt to escape some pain that had become just too much to bear. Turns out, the past is never quite as far away as we’d like to think.
Eventually, Kido’s search led him to a woman who recognized the man from the photograph. Her voice was soft, her words wrapped in regret and longing. She spoke of a time when Daisuke—though he was known by another name back then—was full of hope, before something happened that changed him forever. The details were hazy, but the feelings were crystal clear: loss, betrayal, and the slow unraveling of trust.
